extracted.intended_audience: taxpayers, tax professionals, employers, and other stakeholders responding to proposed Treasury/IRS regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed Treasury/IRS regulations implementing section 224 of the Internal Revenue Code, including a statutorily required list of occupations that customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, definitions of qualified/cash tips, eligibility rules, limitations, and methodology for compiling the occupation list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'qualified tips' (section 224(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified tips mean cash tips received by an individual in an occupation that customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, as provided by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed regulations implement the statutory definition and tie eligibility for the deduction in section 224(a) to occupations listed by the Secretary (the List of Occupations that Receive Tips).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'cash tips' (section 224(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Cash tips' include tips received from customers (paid in cash or charged) and, in the case of an employee, tips received under any tip-sharing arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarified to include checks, credit/debit cards, gift cards, tangible/intangible tokens readily exchangeable for a fixed cash amount (e.g., casino chips), and electronic/mobile payment applications denominated in cash. Excludes items paid in media other than cash or charge (e.g., event tickets, meals, non-exchangeable assets, and most digital assets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms that evidence qualified tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified tips must be included on W-2, Form 1099-NEC, Form 1099-K, Form 1099-MISC, or Form 4137 to be deductible under section 224(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees reporting under TRDA or GITCA using established tip rates are included (their tips show on W-2), and additional tips reported on Form 4137 are also included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of tips reported under TRDA/GITCA agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Tips reported using tip rates under Tipped Employee Participation Agreement (TRDA) or Model Gaming Employee Tip Reporting Agreement (GITCA) count as qualified tips for employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tips are included on Form W-2 per agreement reporting; additional tips reported on Form 4137 are also treated as qualified tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntariness and non-negotiation requirement (224(d)(2)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified tips include only amounts that are paid voluntarily without consequence of nonpayment, are not subject to negotiation, and are determined by the payor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed regulations clarify that tips must be voluntary and not negotiated/payor-determined to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for SSTBs (specified service trade or business)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified tips exclude tips received by an individual who is self-employed in an SSTB or by an employee performing services for an employer operated as an SSTB as defined in section 199A(d)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed regulations explicitly exclude SSTB-related tips from the deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for illegal activity and certain activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified tips do not include tips received while performing a service that is a felony or misdemeanor under applicable law; amounts received for prostitution services and pornographic activity are specifically excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, tips for legal services provided while working for an establishment that violates law in other respects may still qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership/employer-payor relationship exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: A payment is not a 'qualified tip' if the tip recipient has an ownership interest in, or is employed by, the payor of the tip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents treating transfers between owners/employers as deductible qualified tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-employed deduction limitation (section 224(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For self-employed individuals, the deduction for qualified tips is limited to gross income from the trade or business (including qualified tips) minus the sum of deductions allocable to that trade or business (excluding the qualified tips deduction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed regs clarify the deduction itself is not a trade-or-business deduction and is excluded when calculating this limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: SSN and filing-status requirements (section 224(e),(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxpayers must include their Social Security Number (SSN) on the tax return to claim the deduction; taxpayers with only an ITIN cannot use tips to claim the deduction. Married taxpayers must file a joint return for the taxable year to claim the deduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If married, include SSN of the spouse who earned qualified tips; if both spouses earned qualified tips, include both SSNs on the joint return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dollar limitation on the deduction (section 224(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The deduction for qualified tips for any taxable year is limited to $25,000, regardless of filing status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The $25,000 cap applies before the MAGI-based phaseout; taxpayers may rely on proposed regs for taxable years beginning after Dec 31, 2024, until finalization if followed entirely and consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAGI-based phaseout of deduction (section 224(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The deduction is reduced by $100 for each $1,000 by which the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) exceeds $150,000 ($300,000 for joint returns). MAGI is AGI plus amounts excluded under sections 911, 931, or 933.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phaseout is applied after the $25,000 limitation is applied and cannot reduce the deduction below zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupation inclusion standard — frequency threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: An occupation is considered to have customarily and regularly received tips on or before Dec 31, 2024 if individuals in that occupation received cash tips more often than occasionally during a calendar year (i.e., not only on annual holidays or celebrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is informed by prior FLSA guidance but adapted to section 224's statutory language and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of occupations via tip-sharing arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Occupations that do not directly interact with customers may still be included if employees commonly participate in mandatory or voluntary tip-sharing arrangements (e.g., dishwashers participating in tip pools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 224(d)(3)'s inclusive definition of 'cash tips' supports treating tip-sharing recipients as customarily and regularly receiving tips for the deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple data sources to compile occupation list
rubrics_metrics.description: The List of Occupations that Receive Tips was compiled using confidential tax return data (Tax Year 2023), data from GITCA and related IRS programs, the House Budget Committee report on the OBBBA, DOL FLSA guidance and caselaw, and PSID survey data (2017, 2019, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax return data were supplemented because of under-inclusion (independent contractors not on W-2, tips not separately reported on many 1099s) and over-inclusivity (variation/typos in occupation entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum-tip threshold used in statistics (at least $100)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table A statistics report percentages of individuals within SOC-related codes who had at least $100 of tips reported on Form W-2 or Form 4137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The $100 threshold is the metric used for 'percent with reported tips' in the table summarizing Tax Year 2023 single-job holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of Treasury Tipped Occupation Codes (TTOC) and new categorization system
rubrics_metrics.description: To address SOC over-inclusivity and under-inclusivity, Treasury and IRS created a new categorization (TTOC) system: each occupation assigned a three-digit TTOC, title, short description, illustrative examples, and related SOC code(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new system mirrors SOC where appropriate, aggregates multiple SOC detailed codes when needed (e.g., chefs/cooks), and splits SOC codes when they contained both tipped and non-tipped occupations (e.g., chauffeurs moved to 'Taxi and Rideshare Drivers and Chauffeurs' and 'Shuttle Drivers').

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of alternative methods: SOC-only and tax-data-only approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasury/IRS considered but rejected (1) using SOC codes alone and (2) using confidential income tax return data alone because both approaches either omitted occupations that customarily received tips or included occupations that did not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOC codes can be too broad (e.g., 'Animal Caretakers' includes pet caretakers who get tips and zookeepers who generally do not). Tax return data omit independent contractors and are noisy due to occupation entry variation; thus multi-source approach selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistics metrics used to justify inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Table A provides three metrics for each TTOC: percent of individuals with reported tips (>= $100), percent of all reported tips attributable to related SOC codes, and reported tips as percent of wage compensation for tipped workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics were used to characterize tipping intensity across occupations (examples: Bartenders — 82.8% with reported tips; Wait Staff — 34.2% of all reported tips).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of the List of Occupations that Receive Tips
rubrics_metrics.description: The List is organized into broad occupational categories (100s Beverage & Food Service; 200s Entertainment & Events; 300s Hospitality & Guest Services; 400s Home Services; 500s Personal Services; 600s Personal Appearance & Wellness; 700s Recreation & Instruction; 800s Transportation & Delivery) with detailed TTOC entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each TTOC entry includes title, description of services, illustrative examples, and related SOC code(s); taxpayers rely on these TTOCs to determine whether their occupation qualifies for the deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability dates and reliance rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed regulations apply for taxable years beginning after Dec 31, 2024; taxpayers may rely on the proposed regs for such taxable years and until final regs are published provided taxpayers follow the proposed regs in their entirety and consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an interim reliance safe harbor for taxpayers while the rulemaking process concludes.
